recommendations.headline: Call satisfaction - not price - is the strongest predictor of a sale: satisfied calls close at 72% versus 16% for neutral and 6% for dissatisfied calls, yet only 35% of calls (772/2214) are rated satisfied and basic execution gaps (slow/unclear answers in 371 calls, no fixed follow-up in 344, no ask for the order in 208) explain most of the 45% callback/19% order split.
behaviour: Price shopping dominates: price_enquiry is 34% of all intents (755/2214), with 382 calls tagged price_shopper and 232 comparing_quotes across brands.
Most calls end undecided: callback is the top outcome (1006/2214, 45%) versus order (429, 19%) and interested-only (330) - decisions are being deferred, not lost.
Urgency is real but under-served: 294 calls are high urgency and 232 customers are tagged urgent_buyer, while fast_delivery (411) and stock_availability (402) are the top two stated needs.
Price talk rarely even starts: in 70% of calls (1550/2214) price reaction is 'not_discussed', so price objections (310 calls) are not the main blocker to conversation depth.
Repeat business exists but is untapped: 198 calls are repeat_buyer behaviour and only 17 are tagged loyal_to_us and 26 referral - loyalty is not being actively built or asked for.
satisfaction: Only 35% of calls are rated satisfied (772/2214); 52% are neutral (1159) and 8.5% dissatisfied (189) - the neutral bucket is the biggest conversion opportunity since it converts at just 16% vs 72% for satisfied.

Satisfaction correlates far more with winning than any objection: win_pct is 72% when satisfied vs 28% even for the toughest objection category (price_high) - call experience outweighs price sensitivity.
Price is accepted more than it is rejected: 245 calls had price accepted and 348 were negotiating, versus only 71 explicitly 'too_high' - most customers are willing to talk price if engaged well.

Rep execution gaps are large and fixable: slow/unclear answers (371 calls), no fixed follow-up (344), no ask for order (208) and no quote sent (207) are collectively bigger issues than the price_high objection itself (310).

conversion.title: Standardise clear, confident answering on rate/stock queries
conversion.evidence: slow_or_unclear_answer flagged in 371 calls; price_enquiry is 34% of all calls (755) and win_pct drops sharply once a call turns neutral (16%) vs satisfied (72%).
conversion.action: Give reps a quick-reference rate/stock card per product/brand so they can answer in under 30 seconds without hesitation, and train on a confident tone for price and spec questions.

conversion.title: Always fix a concrete follow-up time before ending the call
conversion.evidence: no_follow_up_fixed missed in 344 calls; callback is the top outcome (1006/2214, 45%), meaning almost half of all calls are left open-ended.
conversion.action: Make it mandatory to agree and log an exact day/time for the next contact on every callback, and have managers audit a sample weekly.

conversion.title: Explicitly ask for the order on every price/product call
conversion.evidence: didnt_ask_for_order missed in 208 calls; order outcome is only 19% (429/2214) despite 330 'interested' calls that never converted.
conversion.action: Coach reps to end every quote discussion with a direct closing question (e.g. 'shall I book this for you today?') instead of leaving it open.

conversion.title: Send written quotes immediately, not 'later'
conversion.evidence: no_quote_sent missed in 207 calls; many WhatsApp quote requests in the call log go unanswered or delayed.
conversion.action: Set an SLA (e.g. same-call or within 30 minutes) to send a WhatsApp/PDF quote with specs, and track adherence.

conversion.title: Offer an alternative whenever the exact item/colour/gauge is unavailable
conversion.evidence: didnt_offer_alternative missed in 121 calls; stock_availability is the 2nd biggest objection (301 calls) with only 25% win rate.
conversion.action: Train reps to always propose the nearest matching brand/thickness/colour on the same call rather than ending with 'will check and call back'.

conversion.title: Capture customer segment and requirement details upfront
conversion.evidence: didnt_ask_requirement missed in 89 calls; 796 calls (36%) have segment 'unknown' and convert at only 25% vs 40% for identified dealers.
conversion.action: Add 2-3 quick qualifying questions (segment, project type, quantity) at call start so reps can tailor the pitch and route high-value leads (dealer, builder, contractor) faster.

conversion.title: Lead with value, not just price, when competitor comparison comes up
conversion.evidence: competitor_cheaper objection appears in 80 calls with the lowest win rate among objections (24%); didnt_highlight_value missed in 77 calls.
conversion.action: Equip reps with 2-3 ready value points (JSW authorised distributor, quality assurance, delivery reliability) to counter competitor price comparisons before discounting is even considered.

offers.title: Priority/express delivery slot for urgent orders
offers.why: fast_delivery is the top stated need (411 calls), 232 calls tagged urgent_buyer, and many summaries show same-day/next-morning delivery requests.

offers.title: On-demand cutting/trimming/bending service
offers.for_whom: Fabricators and site customers needing custom lengths
offers.why: cutting_processing need appears in 93 calls; multiple summaries involve bend-length and trim clarifications.

offers.title: Structured short-term credit/performance-invoice option
offers.why: credit_terms objection has the highest win rate among all objections (30%, 66 calls) and needs_credit appears in 85 calls plus credit_period need in 72 calls - indicating real demand that converts well when addressed.

offers.title: Stock-hold/reservation service with confirmation window
offers.for_whom: Customers worried about losing stock to another order
offers.why: stock_availability is the 2nd largest objection (301 calls) and recurring questions include 'will you hold the stock for me?'.

offers.title: Colour-card/sample dispatch service
offers.for_whom: First-time buyers and customers deciding on shade
offers.why: samples need appears in 58 calls, with multiple summaries requesting colour cards or shade photos before purchase.

offers.title: Dedicated site-delivery coordination for bulk/builder orders
offers.why: site_delivery need appears in 88 calls; builder (41%) and contractor (39%) segments already have strong win rates and bulk_buyer behaviour is tagged 200 times.

loyalty.title: Introduce a simple repeat-buyer recognition tier
loyalty.how: Flag customers with 2+ past orders in CRM and give them a named contact point or faster callback priority
loyalty.why: repeat_buyer behaviour is tagged 198 times but loyal_to_us is only 17 - a large base of repeat customers is not being formally recognised.

loyalty.title: Launch a low-key referral acknowledgement program
loyalty.how: Thank and log referred customers, offer them priority handling on their first order
loyalty.why: Only 26 calls are tagged referral; a structured ask ('who else needs roofing sheets?') could grow this.

loyalty.title: Proactive price-change and stock-alert calls/SMS
loyalty.how: Notify regular/dealer customers ahead of known price hikes or new stock arrivals
loyalty.why: regular_updates need appears in 181 calls and several summaries show customers rushing to order 'before the price increase' - advance notice builds trust and urgency.

loyalty.title: Post-delivery check-in call for quality/after-sales support
loyalty.how: A short follow-up call after large or first orders to confirm satisfaction and resolve issues early
loyalty.why: after_sales_support need appears in 40 calls and complaint intent is 158 calls, including colour-mismatch disputes that escalated to threats of complaints.

loyalty.title: Offer test certificates/quality documentation proactively
loyalty.how: Share certification or batch quality info with orders, especially for new or doubtful customers
loyalty.why: quality_assurance need (117 calls) and quality_doubt objection (90 calls, only 27% win) suggest trust-building documentation could lift conversion without discounting.

loyalty.title: Maintain a personal 'preferred supplier' relationship for high-value dealers
loyalty.how: Assign consistent rep contact per top dealer account to build familiarity instead of rotating calls
loyalty.why: Dealers are 48% of all calls (1071) and already convert best (40%) - protecting this relationship via consistency reduces risk of loss to competitors.

non_price_benefits.title: Technical advice and specification guidance
non_price_benefits.why: needs_technical_help is tagged in 328 calls and technical_advice is the 3rd largest stated need (365 calls) - many customers are unsure of gauge/thickness/size and value expert guidance.

non_price_benefits.title: Reliable, consistent stock availability
non_price_benefits.why: stock_availability is both the top need (402 calls) and 2nd largest objection (301 calls) - positioning supply reliability as a differentiator addresses the biggest friction point.

non_price_benefits.title: Fast dispatch and delivery turnaround
non_price_benefits.why: fast_delivery is the single largest stated need (411 calls) and high urgency is tagged in 294 calls.

non_price_benefits.title: Authorised JSW distributor quality assurance
non_price_benefits.why: quality_assurance need (117 calls) and quality_doubt objection (90 calls, lowest-performing at 27% win) show customers want confidence in material quality - authorised distributor status should be stated upfront.

non_price_benefits.title: Flexible credit arrangements for trusted buyers
non_price_benefits.why: credit_terms objection converts better than any other objection (30% win, 66 calls), showing that addressing this directly (not with price cuts) unlocks deals.

non_price_benefits.title: Wide brand and product range (JSW, Pragathi, Radiance, GI, polycarbonate, etc.)
non_price_benefits.why: Top products span 12+ distinct items/brands, letting reps always offer an in-stock alternative instead of losing the call (didnt_offer_alternative missed in 121 calls).

top_questions.question: What is the current rate for [sheet/coil/screw/brand]?
top_questions.answer_tip: Confirm exact thickness, brand and quantity first, give the current rate clearly and immediately follow up with a written quote; mention any announced price change dates for transparency.

top_questions.question: Is [colour/size/thickness] available in stock right now?
top_questions.answer_tip: Check live stock before answering; if unavailable, immediately offer the closest alternative brand/gauge/colour instead of just promising to check and call back.

top_questions.question: When will the delivery vehicle arrive / has it been dispatched?
top_questions.answer_tip: Give a specific date and time window, and proactively message the customer with updates rather than waiting for them to call again.

top_questions.question: Can I get credit or extended payment terms?
top_questions.answer_tip: Explain the credit/performance-invoice process clearly and what's needed to qualify, rather than declining outright - this objection converts well when handled properly.

top_questions.question: Why were the wrong sizes/colours quoted or delivered?
top_questions.answer_tip: Read back all specifications (size, colour, thickness) to the customer before confirming any order to prevent mismatches and rebuild trust if an error occurred.

top_questions.question: Do you have a branch or delivery coverage near my location (e.g. Kerala, Theni, Salem)?
top_questions.answer_tip: Be upfront about service area; if outside normal coverage, offer transport-cost options or refer to the nearest fulfilment point rather than ending the call.

top_questions.question: Is there a price increase coming, and when?
top_questions.answer_tip: Be transparent about any known upcoming change and its effective date - this naturally creates urgency without needing to pressure the customer.

top_questions.question: Can you send the quotation/photo on WhatsApp?
top_questions.answer_tip: Send the quote or image during the call or within a committed short window, and confirm the customer has received it.
